content: This medication may cause a condition that affects the heart's rhythm, known as QT prolongation. The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other medications that can also cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood can further elevate this risk, particularly if you are using certain drugs like diuretics (commonly referred to as water pills) or if you experience conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. Loperamide may cause dizziness or drowsiness. The use of alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can intensify these effects. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages. Liquid forms of this medication may contain sugar and/or alcohol, so caution is advised if you have diabetes, alcohol dependence, or liver disease. Children may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medication, particularly drowsiness, and are at a higher risk of dehydration. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if clearly necessary. While loperamide passes into breast milk, it is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. It is important to keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal products, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. If you are taking this medication on a regular schedule and miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This medication is used to treat sudden diarrhea, including traveler's diarrhea, by slowing down the movement of the gut. This reduces the number of bowel movements and makes the stool less watery. It is also used to reduce the amount of discharge in patients who have had an ileostomy. However, loperamide treats only the symptoms of diarrhea and not its underlying cause, such as an infection. If you are using an over-the-counter product to self-treat, read all the directions on the product package before taking this medication. Take this medication by mouth, usually after each loose stool or as directed by your doctor. The dosage is based on your condition and response to treatment. For children, the dosage is also based on age and weight. Diarrhea can lead to dehydration, so it is important to drink plenty of fluids and replace lost minerals (electrolytes). Contact your doctor immediately if you develop signs of dehydration, such as extreme thirst, decreased urination, muscle cramps, weakness, or fainting. You may also need to switch to a bland diet during this time to reduce irritation to your stomach and intestines. Inform your doctor if your diarrhea does not improve after two days, if your condition worsens, or if you develop new symptoms. Common side effects of this medication include dizziness, drowsiness, tiredness, or constipation. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, remember that they have determined the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking loperamide, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Antibiotics may rarely cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridium difficile (C. difficile). Symptoms include persistent diarrhea, abdominal or stomach pain/cramping, or blood/mucus in your stool. This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Loperamide may worsen this condition. Improper use of this medication, such as overuse or abuse, can cause serious harm, including a fast or irregular heartbeat or death. Do not increase your dose, take it more often, or use it for longer than directed. Taking loperamide with certain other medications may also cause harm. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
